# kernels.minmax_mask_1d { #imcombiners.kernels.minmax_mask_1d }

```python
kernels.minmax_mask_1d(values, *, mask=None, n_min=1, n_max=1, validate=True)
```

Reject the `n_min` smallest and `n_max` largest unmasked values at each pixel. Single-pass (1-D mask-only variant).

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**values**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [(ndarray, shape(N))]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   One-dimensional value vector. Accepted dtypes are `uint8`, `uint16`, `int16`, `int32`, `float32`, and `float64`. Integer inputs are promoted to the package's floating workspace when `validate` is `True`.

<code>[**mask**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [ndarray of bool]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Input mask; `True` means already masked. Must have shape ``(N,)``.

<code>[**n_min**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int or float]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [1]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Number of minimum-side values to reject at each pixel. Values ``>= 1`` are treated as a frame count. Values in ``[0, 1)`` are treated as a fraction of the total frame count ``N`` and converted via ``int(N * n_min + 0.001)``, matching IRAF's internal fraction arithmetic.

<code>[**n_max**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [int or float]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [1]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Same convention as `n_min`, applied to the maximum-side tail.

<code>[**validate**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [True]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   If `True`, check dimensionality and normalize dtype/contiguity before entering the Rust kernel. If `False`, callers must provide inputs that satisfy the compiled kernel assumptions.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[**mask_rej**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [ndarray of bool, shape (N,)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   `True` for excluded samples, including input masks and non-finite values.

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

Sort the `M` finite, unmasked samples at each output pixel. With `N`
the original image count, a request `a` (`n_min` or `n_max`) resolves to::

    A = int(N * a + 0.001) if 0 <= a < 1 else int(a)
    k = int(M * A / N + 0.001)

Reject `k` samples from that tail, first the low tail, then the high tail
of the remaining values. Both counts use the initial `M`; available samples
limit the cuts. Thus masked/non-finite inputs reduce even count-based requests
proportionally. For example, ``N=10, M=5, n_min=2`` removes one minimum.
This is rank selection, not a value threshold: tied values may be split.
There is no spread estimate or iteration; `low`/`upp` are retained extrema.
For derivations and worked examples, see the [Rejection Methods tutorial](https://ysbach.github.io/imcombiners/tutorials/05-rejection-methods.html).
